definitions.explanation: Low in price. A formal or written-style word that can be neutral or slightly negative depending on context. When describing price alone, it is neutral; when implying low quality, it carries a negative nuance.

examples.japanese: {安価|あんか}な{商品|しょうひん}を{探|さが}す。
{安価|あんか}で{品質|ひんしつ}のいい{素材|そざい}が{手|て}に{入|はい}った。
examples.english: I got my hands on an inexpensive yet high-quality material.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}から{安価|あんか}な{労働力|ろうどうりょく}を{輸入|ゆにゅう}することの{問題点|もんだいてん}が{議論|ぎろん}されている。
examples.english: The problems of importing cheap labor from overseas are being debated.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal alternative to {安|やす}い. Commonly used in writing, business contexts, and news reports. Unlike {安|やす}い, which is purely conversational and neutral, {安価|あんか} can carry a slight implication of low quality when used to describe goods, though this depends on context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {安価|あんか}な{商品|しょうひん}: inexpensive goods
- {安価|あんか}に{提供|ていきょう}する: to offer at a low price
- {安価|あんか}な{労働力|ろうどうりょく}: cheap labor
- {安価|あんか}で{高品質|こうひんしつ}: cheap and high quality

SIMILAR WORDS:
{安|やす}い is the everyday word for "cheap/inexpensive." {安価|あんか} is more formal and often used in written or business contexts. {廉価|れんか} is even more formal and literary.
